Subject: Score variance debrief and comms draft

Team —

I finished a first pass reconciling Q2 OKR scores against the evidence packs. Two quick notes:

- Several cross-functional objectives show >15% variance between manager-proposed scores and audit-adjusted scores (notably Platform SLOs and Hosting Cost).
- The narrative the Growth team drafted leans positive but glosses over the cost regression (we should not ignore it in the exec summary).

Attached: Q2_score_audit.xlsx (pivot by objective), I tucked the raw comments into the file.

Asks:
1) Sean / Vivek — can you triage the Platform SLO variance this afternoon? The raw logs are in the evidence pack request (I flagged the most material cases).
2) Monica — can you produce a short evidence summary per-objective (one paragraph each) that we can drop into the QBR narrative?
3) Laura (me) — I’ll draft a one-paragraph executive line for the QBR once we have sign-off on any score adjustments.

I’ve copied Sarah at Acme (they asked to see the high-level score mechanics) — we should avoid sending anything with raw PII.

Thanks,

--
Laura Bennett
VP, Strategy & Ops
Redwood Inference

Laura — thanks for pulling this together. Quick reactions: 

- I agree we need to reconcile Platform SLOs first; if the telemetry shows an uptick in tail latency for one service, that should be explicit in the evidence paragraph.
- For Hosting Cost, we should separate infra spend increases (one-offs like migration) vs. steady-state unit cost regressions. Try to make that distinction in the evidence summary.

I can take point on the SLO variance. I’ll run the spike queries and post a short log excerpt into the evidence pack by 4pm.

Monica — once you have the per-objective one-paragraphs, put them into narrative_draft.md and flag any items that require a score change. We should limit score changes to cases where the evidence weight clearly contradicts the manager justification.

We should also prepare a short comms draft for execs that:
- States the final score and top rationale (1 line)
- Calls out 2–3 high-impact regressions and remediation plan
- Notes any contested scores and next steps for follow-up (owner + date)

I’m on a call 2–3pm PT but will review the updates after.

Thanks —
Sean

Subject: Re: Score variance debrief and comms draft

Folks — attached: evidence_pack.pdf and narrative_draft.md. I pushed an evidence paragraph for each objective into the draft. Highlights: 

- Platform SLOs (Obj P1): Audit found three incidents in May that drove sustained 99th-percentile increases; manager justification emphasized mitigations but did not quantify user impact. Recommendation: reduce from 8 -> 6.
- Hosting Cost (Obj C3): One-time migration invoice (May) accounts for ~40% of quarter spend spike; baseline unit cost actually increased ~6% vs prior quarter. Recommendation: score remains 7 but annotate in narrative; track as FYI with remediation owner (Infra: Karthik).
- Product Velocity (Obj R2): Evidence aligns with manager score; no change.

I also added a short appendix with links to the raw logs (redacted) and a snippet of the billing line items.

Inline excerpt (narrative_draft.md):
"Q2 saw strong delivery on product roadmap objectives, offset by platform reliability slips and one-off migration costs that increased hosting spend in May. While product velocity met target expectations, the platform regressions materially affected high-percentile latency for two customer-facing endpoints; remediation plans are in place and rates are expected to normalize by Q3."

Please flag any disagreement inline. I’ll update the spreadsheet if we finalize any score changes.

Thanks —
Monica

--
Monica Patel
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
